security_audit.summary: The 26 backtick alerts are Markdown formatting, while the example URL, local workflow path, and scoped GITHUB_TOKEN are benign template constructs. The AWS example promotes long-lived cloud credentials, and mutable third-party action references create a high-confidence CI supply-chain risk. Replace static AWS keys and pin actions before publication.

remediation.issue: The Kubernetes deployment example authenticates with long-lived AWS access keys.
remediation.suggestion: Use GitHub OIDC with a restricted AWS role, grant id-token permission, and remove both static access-key inputs.

remediation.issue: Third-party actions use mutable major-version and master references.
remediation.suggestion: Pin every third-party action to a reviewed full commit SHA and maintain those pins with automated dependency updates.

content.value_statement: Creating reliable CI/CD workflows requires careful triggers, permissions, caching, secrets, and deployment controls. This skill provides adaptable patterns for testing, containers, Kubernetes, matrices, scanning, and approvals.
actual_capabilities: Provides a Node.js test workflow with version matrices, dependency caching, linting, tests, and coverage upload.
Provides a Docker build and GHCR publishing workflow with metadata, labels, and GitHub Actions caching.
Shows an AWS EKS deployment sequence using kubeconfig updates, Kubernetes apply, rollout checks, and service inspection.
Shows Python matrix testing across three operating systems and four Python versions.
Demonstrates reusable workflows with typed inputs and inherited repository secrets.
Includes Trivy, Snyk, deployment environment metadata, and Slack notification patterns.
limitations: Every template requires repository-specific changes to branches, commands, environments, permissions, and secret names.
The skill does not validate workflow syntax, repository settings, cloud roles, or deployment results.
The AWS example uses long-lived credentials and should be replaced with GitHub OIDC.
Referenced asset and resource files are absent; only the inline patterns in SKILL.md are available.

use_cases.title: Add Application CI

use_cases.title: Publish and Deploy Services

use_cases.title: Introduce Pipeline Scanning

prompt_templates.title: Create a Test Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a GitHub Actions test workflow for [runtime] versions [versions]. Run [install command], [lint command], and [test command] on pull requests.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a repository without continuous integration.

prompt_templates.title: Build and Publish a Container
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a workflow that builds [image name] from [context] and publishes it to [registry]. Use least-privilege permissions and branch-based tags.
prompt_templates.scenario: Container publishing from the main branch.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Reusable Matrix Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a reusable workflow for [language] across [operating systems] and [versions]. Define typed inputs, required secrets, caching, tests, and artifact retention.

prompt_templates.title: Secure a Production Deployment
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a production workflow for [platform]. Use immutable action pins, OIDC authentication, scoped permissions, approvals, concurrency controls, rollback checks, and deployment verification.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced deployment with cloud access and protected environments.

output_examples.input: Create Node.js CI for versions 18 and 20 with npm caching, linting, tests, and coverage.
output_examples.output: A pull request workflow outline with a two-version matrix, npm cache configuration, ordered quality checks, and coverage publishing.

output_examples.input: Build and publish my service image to GitHub Container Registry after changes reach main.
output_examples.output: A container workflow outline with restricted package permissions, registry authentication, metadata tags, layer caching, and main-branch publishing.

output_examples.input: Deploy tagged releases to Amazon EKS with approval and short-lived credentials.
output_examples.output: A protected deployment outline using GitHub OIDC, an AWS role, immutable actions, Kubernetes rollout verification, and failure reporting.

best_practices: Pin third-party actions to reviewed commit SHAs and update them through controlled dependency automation.
Grant each job only required permissions and prefer short-lived OIDC credentials over stored cloud keys.
Validate generated workflows in a nonproduction repository before enabling package publishing or deployment.
anti_patterns: Do not copy placeholder branches, regions, cluster names, namespaces, or commands into production unchanged.
Do not expose deployment secrets to untrusted pull request workflows or broadly privileged third-party actions.
Do not use mutable master refs or assume major-version tags provide immutable supply-chain protection.

faq.question: Does this skill create complete workflows?
faq.answer: It provides inline patterns that an assistant can adapt. Repository commands, permissions, environments, and secrets still require user input.

faq.question: Which technology stacks are covered?
faq.answer: Examples cover Node.js, Python, Docker, GitHub Container Registry, AWS EKS, Kubernetes, Trivy, Snyk, and Slack notifications.

faq.question: Can it create reusable workflows?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a workflow_call pattern with a typed Node.js version input and a required secret.

faq.question: Are the examples ready for production?
faq.answer: No. Review action pins, permissions, credentials, commands, environment protection, and repository settings before production use.

faq.question: How should AWS authentication be configured?
faq.answer: Prefer GitHub OIDC and a narrowly scoped AWS role. Avoid persistent access keys when federation is available.

faq.question: Are referenced asset files included?
faq.answer: No. The audited package contains only SKILL.md, so the listed asset and reference paths are unavailable.
